Much of what the diamond mines of Mirny need, from fuel to machinery, comes upriver by barge in the short summer and is unloaded here for the long road north. Until 1963 the town was called Mukhtuya.
Q157493.w: A town strung along a wide river winding through endless taiga, with a road heading north through the forest.
f: The Lena, about 4,400 km long, is one of the longest rivers in the world.
Mirny, the diamond town supplied through Lensk, lies about 200 km to the north.
The river is navigable here only in the ice-free months, roughly from late May to October.

q.q: What was Lensk called until 1963?

Q103273.t: A gold-rush town named after an 'unnoticeable' creek
Q103273.s: Rounded, forested hills of the Aldan Highlands roll away in every direction, scarred here and there by old gold workings. In 1923 prospectors found gold beside a stream called Nezametny, 'the unnoticeable one', and a rush followed. The town that grew up took the stream's name and became Aldan only in 1939. The railway and highway to Yakutsk now pass through it.
Q103273.w: A small town in rolling, forested highlands, with a railway and a road running north through the taiga.
f: Aldan was founded in 1923 beside a newly found gold deposit and became a town in 1932.
Despite its name, the town stands not on the Aldan river but on a small stream in the Aldan Highlands.
The Amur–Yakutsk railway runs through Aldan on its way north towards Yakutsk.

q.q: What was Aldan called until 1939?

Q721374.t: A far-north town that lit its streets first
Q721374.s: Hammerfest clings to a bay on the island of Kvaløya, among bare, rounded hills above the Norwegian Sea. It is one of the northernmost towns in the world: the sun does not set from mid-May to late July, and in midwinter it does not rise. Just offshore, on the islet of Melkøya, gas from beneath the Barents Sea is chilled into liquid for shipping.
Q721374.w: A small town around a bay on a bare, hilly island, with an industrial plant on an islet just offshore.
f: In 1891 Hammerfest became the first town in Northern Europe with electric street lighting.
The Meridian Column here marks the northern end of the Struve Geodetic Arc, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Melkøya plant, opened in 2007, was Europe's first large liquefied natural gas export plant.

q.q: What does Hammerfest's Meridian Column mark?
q.a: The end of the Struve Geodetic Arc

Q1025866.t: A gold town in the frozen heart of Yakutia
Q1025866.s: Deep among the bare ridges of the Chersky Range, the Nera flows into the Indigirka, and Ust-Nera takes its name from that meeting point. It is the centre of the Oymyakon district, one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth, where winter temperatures often fall below −50 °C. Gold brought people here, and the Kolyma Highway crosses the Indigirka by the settlement.
Q1025866.w: A small settlement where two rivers meet in a wide valley among bare, often snowy mountain ridges.
f: Ust-Nera is the administrative centre of the Oymyakon district, known as a pole of cold.
A concrete bridge carrying the Kolyma Highway across the Indigirka opened here in 1978.
Gold mining is the main industry around Ust-Nera.

q.q: Which river does the Nera flow into at Ust-Nera?

Q7054.t: A mountain mining town famous for its crystals
Q7054.s: A narrow valley in the forested Sikhote-Alin mountains holds Dalnegorsk, about 30 km from the Sea of Japan. The hills around it are riddled with ore: lead, zinc and boron have been mined here for decades. To mineral collectors worldwide, the name means superb crystals, from glassy calcite to pale green datolite. Until 1972 the town was called Tetyukhe.
Q7054.w: A small town strung along a narrow valley in forested mountains, with a river running south-east to the sea.
f: Dalnegorsk is the only place in Russia where boron is mined.
The boron plant at Dalnegorsk began work in 1965.
The Rudnaya river flows from the town to the Sea of Japan.

q.q: What was Dalnegorsk called until 1972?

Q648799.t: Russia's first foothold on the Pacific
Q648799.s: A low, narrow spit between the open sea and a shallow estuary carries Okhotsk, where the Okhota and Kukhtuy rivers reach the coast. Founded in 1647, it was the first Russian settlement on the Pacific shore, and for more than a century its main port for voyages to Kamchatka and Alaska. Behind it, flat, lake-dotted lowland runs to low hills.
Q648799.w: A small settlement on a thin spit between a wide sea and a river estuary, backed by flat lowland and low hills.
f: For about half the year the sea off Okhotsk is covered with ice.
Vitus Bering's expeditions built ships at Okhotsk in the 18th century.
The Sea of Okhotsk is named after the town, and the town after the Okhota river.

q.q: Which explorer's expeditions built ships at Okhotsk?

Q2359080.t: A tiny town next to a giant permafrost scar
Q2359080.s: About 10 km south-east of Batagay, look for a pale, tadpole-shaped scar on a forested hillside: the Batagaika crater, a slump about 1 km long where the permafrost is thawing. Each summer its cliffs retreat further, exposing ice and soil tens of thousands of years old. Batagay itself sits on the Yana, in one of the coldest corners of Yakutia.
Q2359080.w: A small settlement on a river in taiga, with a large, pale, tadpole-shaped scar on a hillside to the south-east.
f: The Batagaika crater is about 1 km long, around 800 m wide and in places 50–100 m deep.
The crater began as a small gully after the forest on the slope was cleared in the 1960s, and has grown ever since.
Batagay is the centre of the Verkhoyansk district, one of the coldest places in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.q: What is the Batagaika crater near Batagay?

Q1003237.t: A coal-mining settlement in the Transbaikal hills
Q1003237.s: Low, forested ridges of Transbaikalia roll to the horizon, larch and pine on the slopes and open meadows in the valleys. In one of those valleys lies Bukachacha, which grew up around a coal mine opened in 1930. A branch railway carried its coal south to the Trans-Siberian. The mine closed in 1998, and the settlement has been shrinking ever since.
Q1003237.w: A small settlement in a valley among rolling, forested ridges, with a railway line heading off to the south.
f: The Bukachacha coal mine began work in November 1930.
A railway branch from Chernyshevsk, on the Trans-Siberian, reached the settlement in 1932.
In 1979 Bukachacha had more than 9,000 inhabitants.

q.q: What was mined at Bukachacha?

Q1305638.t: Chukotka's airport settlement across the estuary
Q1305638.s: Across the wide Anadyr estuary from Anadyr, on a flat, lake-dotted shore of tundra, sits Ugolnye Kopi, whose name means 'coal mines'. It began in 1929 as a miners' settlement on a brown-coal deposit that fuelled Anadyr. Today it is best known for the airport serving Chukotka's capital: passengers cross the estuary by boat in summer and over the ice in winter.
Q1305638.w: A small settlement on flat tundra beside a wide estuary, with a long runway nearby and a town on the opposite shore.
f: The settlement was founded in 1929 beside a brown-coal deposit.
Ugolny airport, beside the settlement, serves Anadyr, the capital of Chukotka.
Brown-coal mining remains the settlement's main industry.

q.q: Which city does the airport at Ugolnye Kopi serve?

Q2621673.t: An old Cossack fort just past the Arctic Circle
Q2621673.s: A giant of a river, kilometres wide and braided with sandy islands, the Lena flows north here through larch taiga towards the Arctic Ocean. Zhigansk stands on its left bank, just north of the Arctic Circle. Cossacks built a fort here in 1632, the same year Yakutsk was founded, which makes it one of the oldest Russian settlements in Yakutia.
Q2621673.w: A small village on the west bank of a huge river full of sandy islands, with larch forest all around.
f: In 1783 Zhigansk became a district town, but it lost that status in 1805.
Zhigansk is the centre of a district where many Evenks live.

q.q: In which year was the fort at Zhigansk founded?

Q918830.t: The last stop before the North Pole
Q918830.s: Far out on the Taymyr tundra, the Khatanga river winds towards the Laptev Sea, and on its high bank stands the settlement of the same name. It began in the 17th century as a winter outpost for collecting fur tribute. Today its long runway makes it a staging point for expeditions to the North Pole, and a museum here keeps mammoth remains found in the frozen ground.
Q918830.w: A small settlement on the high bank of a broad river winding across flat tundra dotted with lakes.
f: Khatanga was founded in 1626.
Khatanga's mammoth museum opened in 2007.
Cellars dug into the permafrost of the riverbank stay below freezing all year round.

q.q: Khatanga is a staging point for expeditions to where?

Q2312088.t: A tundra outpost on the lower Indigirka
Q2312088.s: Beyond the Arctic Circle, the lower Indigirka winds across tundra so riddled with lakes that there seems to be more water than land. Chokurdakh stands on the river's left bank, the centre of a vast and almost empty district. Nearby, the Kytalyk protected area guards a nesting ground of the Siberian white crane, one of the rarest birds on Earth.
Q2312088.w: A small settlement on a big river crossing flat tundra covered with countless round lakes.
f: Chokurdakh is the centre of the Allaikhovsky district, which covers more than 100,000 km².
The Indigirka reaches the East Siberian Sea through a delta north of the settlement.
Kytalyk, near Chokurdakh, is world-famous as a nesting place of the Siberian crane.

q.q: Which rare bird nests in the Kytalyk area near Chokurdakh?

Q237.t: The world's smallest country, inside a city
Q237.s: Inside Rome, a short way west of the Tiber, lies a walled patch less than a kilometre across: Vatican City, the smallest country in the world. It covers about 44 hectares, less than many city parks. From cruise height it is only a speck within the sprawl of Rome, yet it has its own government, flag, stamps and even a railway station.
Q237.w: A tiny walled patch in the western part of Rome, a short way west of the Tiber — too small to pick out easily.
f: At about 0.44 km², Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
The dome of St Peter's Basilica, designed by Michelangelo, rises to about 136 m.
The Swiss Guard has protected the Pope since 1506.

q.q: Since which year has the Swiss Guard protected the Pope?
